ogTitle: Where to Stay in Chaweng, Koh Samui
ogDesc: The best hotels in Chaweng by budget.
intro: Chaweng is the area most first-time visitors to Samui book, because it bundles the island's longest white-sand beach, restaurants of every kind, the Central mall, and a beach-road strip full of bars and clubs into one place. Roughly, it splits into the central stretch around Central, which is busy and handy for food and shopping, and the quieter northern end (Chaweng Noi) and southern tip, where the water is shallower and more family-friendly. One thing to know: the nightlife along central Chaweng runs loud into the early hours, so light sleepers should move toward the ends of the beach or ask for an inward-facing room. Getting around the island means songthaews, taxis, or a rented scooter, as there's no strong public transit. The picks below run from a social beachfront hostel to luxury pool-villa resorts.

blocks.html: Short answer: Chaweng is Koh Samui's main and liveliest beach, bundling a long stretch of sand, restaurants, the Central mall, and a nightlife strip into one spot. Stays run from a few-hundred-baht beachfront hostel to seafront pool villas in the multi-thousands. Pick the central stretch if you want to walk to everything, or the quieter southern end if you want calm. Rates start around ฿650 and climb into the low five figures.

items.name: Lub d Koh Samui Chaweng Beach
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Budget · meeting people · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A design-led beachfront hostel from the Lub d chain, with both dorms and private rooms. The highlight is an infinity pool right on the sand with a swim-up bar, plus nightly events like parties and DJ sets. It scores around 9.3 in reviews for its seafront spot and fun atmosphere. Best for solo travellers or groups of friends who want to meet people. The trade-offs: it sits in the nightlife zone so expect noise, and dorms aren't for anyone after quiet.

items.name: COSI Samui Chaweng Beach
items.meta: ★ 3-star · Best for: Value · next to Central mall · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: An affordable lifestyle hotel from the Centara group, right next to CentralFestival mall and about a 5-minute walk to Chaweng Beach. The selling points are a rooftop pool with a see-through edge, clean modern rooms, and free daily credit for a drink and a bite at the in-house café. Reviews sit around 8.0, praising the cleanliness and friendly staff. A good fit for budget-minded travellers who want to be near food and shopping and don't mind a short walk to the sand.

items.name: Chaweng Regent Beach Resort
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Value · beachfront in central Chaweng · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A resort set directly on the central stretch of Chaweng Beach, an easy walk to restaurants, bars, and the mall. The highlights are two pools set in gardens, a beach bar, and a kids' club and spa. Rooms and bungalows spread across a large site. Reviews sit around 4.2 out of 5, praising the location and helpful staff. A solid pick for anyone who wants a beachfront resort close to everything in Chaweng, with the trade-off that you're in the middle of the busy zone.

items.name: Banana Fan Sea Resort
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Beachfront · quieter southern end · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A beachfront resort on the quieter southern tip of Chaweng, still walkable to shops and the central area. The draws are the fine white sand out front, a seaside infinity pool, and free activities like cooking classes and yoga. It has 70 Thai-style rooms and bungalows. Reviews are very strong at around 4.7 out of 5, ranking it near the top in Chaweng, with praise for cleanliness and warm service. Ideal for couples or families who want sand at the door without being in the middle of the noise.

items.name: Buri Rasa Village Samui
items.meta: ★ 4-star · Best for: Couples · adults-only beachfront boutique · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: An adults-only beachfront boutique resort on Chaweng (guests aged 16 and over), styled in Southern Thai design. The highlights are a calm, romantic mood, an outdoor pool, a spa, and a beachside restaurant. It's positioned a one-minute walk to the sea and close to central Chaweng. Reviews are high and it ranks near the top in the area, with praise for the beautiful spacious rooms and the service. Best for couples or honeymooners who want beachfront privacy without children around.

items.name: SALA Samui Chaweng Beach Resort
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Luxury · seafront pool villas · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A five-star, design-forward resort on Chaweng Beach. The selling point is the large number of rooms and suites with their own private pools, especially the oceanfront wing where every villa has a private pool and sea view. There are two main pools, a spa, and restaurants. Reviews praise the attentive service, the spacious luxurious rooms, and a strong breakfast. Best for couples or anyone wanting villa-level privacy by the sea. It's noticeably pricier than the Chaweng average.

items.name: Centara Reserve Samui
items.meta: ★ 5-star · Best for: Luxury · quiet end with large grounds · 🔎 Find a deal on Agoda
items.blurb: A luxury resort on a quieter part of Chaweng Beach (formerly Centara Grand, now reimagined), set in large seafront grounds. The highlights are two pools, one an adults-only beachside infinity pool and the other a family pool, plus pool villas, several restaurants, and a spa. Rooms blend colonial and modern design. Reviews praise the service and the attention to detail. Best for families or couples who want a full-service resort in a calmer spot than central Chaweng.

faq.q: In Chaweng, should I stay on the central stretch or at the ends of the beach?
faq.a: It depends on your priority. The central stretch around Central, like Chaweng Regent or COSI, is handiest for restaurants, bars, and the mall, ideal if you want things to do nearby, but it's loud at night. The southern end, like Banana Fan Sea, or a beachfront boutique like Buri Rasa, is quieter with shallower water, better for couples and families. If you want the calmest spot and have the budget, look at a luxury resort toward the end of the beach like Centara Reserve.

faq.q: Is Chaweng very noisy at night, and is it hard to sleep?
faq.a: Central Chaweng, the bar-and-club zone, runs loud into the early hours, since it's the island's main nightlife area. If you book within that radius, ask for a higher floor or an inward-facing room, which helps. A hostel like Lub d, right by the nightlife, suits party-goers more than anyone after quiet. If you don't sleep easily, move toward the southern or northern ends of the beach, where the calmer resorts are.

faq.q: Is it easy to get around Chaweng and the rest of Samui, and do I need to rent a vehicle?
faq.a: Within Chaweng itself, walking is easy since the restaurants, bars, and mall are close together. But for other beaches, the airport, or sights around the island, there's no strong public transit. Most people use songthaews (shared pickups where you agree the fare before boarding), taxis, Grab, or a hotel car. If you plan several days of island sightseeing, renting a scooter is more flexible and cheaper, though some roads are busy and traffic moves fast, so take care if you're not used to it.
